chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr from Abu al-Walid said:

I was sitting with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Najiyah Abu Habib asked him, saying: 'May I be your ransom, O Messenger of God, I have a mill in which I grind grain, and sometimes I stand during a part of the night, and I recognize from the mill that the servant has slept, so I strike the wall to wake him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, you are in God's obedience, seeking His provision.'

key_terms.رَحًى: A millstone or mill used for grinding grain
key_terms.نَاجِيَةُ: A companion of the Imams, known as Najiyah

ai.seo_question: Is waking a servant to work at night considered an act of worship?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Najiyah Abu Habib inquires whether the physical exertion of waking a servant to grind grain for sustenance at night holds spiritual merit. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that such diligent labor, undertaken to secure lawful provision (rizq), is itself an act of obedience to God, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the sanctity of worldly work when performed with the intention of fulfilling one's duties.
